title: Subcontractor Safety
summary: On a multi-contractor site, everyone shares responsibility for safety. OSHA explains who is responsible for what, and which employers can be held responsible for a hazard.
talking_points: A prime contractor and its subcontractors may divide jobsite duties by agreement, such as who provides first-aid facilities, but the prime contractor keeps overall responsibility for compliance (29 CFR 1926.16(a)).
A prime contractor who accepts full performance of a contract takes on all employer obligations under OSHA's construction standards, including for subcontracted work (1926.16(b)).
A subcontractor is responsible for compliance for the part of the work it takes on, so responsibility is joint (1926.16(c)).
Prime contractors and subcontractors at any tier can be subject to enforcement (1926.16(d)).

OSHA's multi-employer policy names four kinds of employer: creating (caused the hazard), exposing (its own workers are exposed), correcting (responsible for fixing the hazard) and controlling (has general supervisory authority over the site).

An exposing employer must protect its workers. If it cannot correct a hazard itself, it must ask the employer who can, tell its employees and take reasonable protective steps, such as personal fall protection.
A controlling employer must use reasonable care to prevent and find violations, including by inspecting at a suitable frequency and enforcing its rules.
Good practice: know which role your company plays on this site, and tell the controlling contractor about any hazard another trade creates.
site_hazards_to_check: Hazard created by one trade that exposes another trade's workers
No clear agreement on who provides first aid, inspections and safety equipment
Nobody responsible for inspecting shared areas
Subcontractor crews that were not briefed on site rules
Hazard reported but nobody assigned to correct it
discussion_questions: Which roles does our company hold on this job, and who is the controlling employer?
What do we do when another trade's work puts our crew at risk?
Who inspects the shared areas, and how often?
